sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Nebular Hypothesis**: The leading model explaining the formation of the solar system, stating that it collapsed from a giant rotating gas cloud (solar nebula).
• **Barycentric Orbit**: Planets do not revolve around the exact center of the Sun, but rather around the **barycenter**, the common center of mass.
• **Frost Line (Snow Line)**: The distance in the solar nebula from the proto-Sun where volatile compounds like water, ammonia, and methane condensed into solid ice grains, separating terrestrial and jovian planets.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The Sun contains **99.86%** of the total mass of the known solar system, dominating its gravitational dynamics.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: High density, rocky composition, few or no moons, thin or dense secondary atmospheres, located inside the asteroid belt.
Proximity to the solar heat stripped away lighter gases during formation; intense solar wind.
High frequency in Prelims regarding surface temperatures, retrograde rotation (Venus), and atmospheric compositions.
Jovian / Gas Giants (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune)
Low density, massive size, hydrogen-helium composition, ring systems, numerous satellites, located beyond the frost line.
Accumulation of massive volatile gas envelopes due to lower temperatures and abundant raw materials.
Tested on ring structures, magnetic fields, and Galilean satellites.
Dwarf Planets (Pluto, Eris, Haumea, Makemake, Ceres)
Orbit the Sun, massive enough to be rounded by gravity, but have not cleared their orbital neighborhood.
IAU Resolution 2006 reclassification criteria based on dynamical dominance.
Tricky Prelims options regarding exact IAU definition and location of Ceres (Asteroid Belt) vs. Pluto (Kuiper Belt).

items.definition: A circumstellar disc in the outer solar system, extending from the orbit of Neptune to approximately 50 AU from the Sun, containing icy planetesimals and short-period comets.
A theoretical spherical shell of predominantly icy planetesimals believed to surround the Sun at a distance of up to 100,000 AU, serving as the origin of long-period comets.
The minimum distance to which a celestial body, held together only by its own gravity, can approach a second body without being torn apart by tidal forces.
The global authority responsible for naming and classifying celestial bodies, famous for formally defining a 'planet' in Prague (2006).

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Asteroid Belt**: Located between Mars and Jupiter (~2.2 to 3.2 AU); contains remnant planetesimals prevented from forming a planet due to Jupiter's powerful gravitational perturbations.
• **Heliopause**: The boundary where the Sun's solar wind is stopped by the interstellar medium; marks the practical edge of the solar system.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Space debris management, orbital congestion in Low Earth Orbit (LEO), and radiation hazards for interplanetary missions.
• **Policy Interventions**: UN Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space (COPUOS) guidelines, planetary protection policies, and ISRO's orbital debris tracking initiatives.

items.title: Mnemonic for Classification / Sequence
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Noodles"
• **Decoded Meaning**: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly verifies planet sequence from closest to farthest from the Sun, preventing mix-ups between Uranus and Neptune.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Density decreases outward: Terrestrial planets have high densities (~4-5 g/cm³), while Gas Giants have low densities (Saturn is less dense than water at ~0.69 g/cm³).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that Pluto was removed from the solar system. Correction: Pluto was removed from the list of *planets*, but it remains a core member of the solar system classified as a *dwarf planet*.

Mains Value Addition: In questions concerning space technology or geophysics, link planetary differentiation and magnetic field generation (dynamo effect) to Earth's unique habitable zone (Goldilocks Zone).

keyTakeaways: The solar system is sharply divided into terrestrial (rocky) and jovian (gaseous) planets separated by the asteroid belt and the frost line.
The IAU 2006 criteria require a celestial body to orbit the Sun, be hydrostatically rounded, and clear its neighborhood to be classified as a planet.
Deep space regions like the Kuiper Belt and Oort Cloud hold critical clues about the primordial composition and evolution of the solar nebula.
